relations: number (Char, unique constraint, E164-sanitized on create/write)

behavioral_notes.observation: phone_validation extends the abstract 'base' model so EVERY Odoo model gains _phone_format(fname/number/country/force_format='E164'). With no explicit number it ensure_one()s, picks the first non-empty field from _phone_get_number_fields() (whichever of 'mobile','phone' exist on the model), infers a country via _phone_get_country() (record country_id field -> else customer-partner country via _mail_get_partner_fields -> else env.company.country_id), then delegates to the phone_validation.phone_format tool. raise_exception=False (default) swallows UserError and returns False, so callers get either a clean E164 string or False. None of this dispatch is visible in metadata.

The pure-Python helper wraps the external `phonenumbers` library: phone_parse() calls phonenumbers.parse() twice (raw, then on the INTERNATIONAL-formatted result to apply metadata patches), then runs is_possible_number / is_possible_number_with_reason and is_valid_number, raising UserError for INVALID_COUNTRY_CODE / TOO_SHORT / invalid prefix and self-healing TOO_LONG inputs typed as '0033...' or '33...' by retrying with a '+' prefix. phone_format() renders to one of E164(0)/INTERNATIONAL(1)/NATIONAL(2)/RFC3966(3) — NATIONAL only when the parsed country_code matches the passed country_phone_code, otherwise it falls back to INTERNATIONAL. phone_get_region_data_for_number infers ISO code + national number + dial code from a bare number. All checksum/length/region rules live in the phonenumbers metadata, invisible to the ORM.

behavioral_notes.element: graceful fallback when `phonenumbers` is missing (tools/phone_validation.py except ImportError)
behavioral_notes.observation: The entire helper module is wrapped in try: import phonenumbers / except ImportError. When the library is absent, phone_format() logs a one-time _logger.info ('contact numbers will not be verified') and returns the number UNCHANGED, phone_parse() returns False, and the region helpers return empty strings — so phone_validation degrades to a no-op pass-through instead of crashing dependent modules (crm/sms/event). The dependency is NOT declared in __manifest__ external_dependencies, making `phonenumbers` an optional/soft requirement.

The mixin stores a computed phone_sanitized (E164) recomputed via dynamic @api.depends(_phone_get_sanitize_triggers -> number fields + country field + partner fields) and computes phone_sanitized_blacklisted/phone_blacklisted by matching against phone.blacklist (sudo). init() programmatically CREATEs a btree + (if pg_trgm available) GIN trigram expression index on regexp-stripped phone/mobile columns to make _search_phone_mobile_search fast. These DB-level side-effects and the cross-model blacklist join exist only in Python/SQL.

phone.blacklist.create() re-sanitizes every incoming number through env.user._phone_format (raise_exception=True) and re-activates an existing inactive entry instead of duplicating (unique(number) constraint); _remove archives via action_archive (active=False) rather than deleting; both log chatter via mail.thread. res.users._deactivate_portal_user(request_blacklist=True) auto-adds the deleted portal user's phone numbers to the blacklist with an audit message — a GDPR-style opt-out side-effect not shown by metadata.

No frontend assets: present=false, 0 JS files, 0 XML templates, 0 OWL components, 0 registry registrations, 0 patches, no asset bundles. All behaviour is server-side (ORM compute/onchange/SQL search + phonenumbers wrapper). The only UI is the static QWeb form/list/search views for phone.blacklist plus the inherited res.partner form; live formatting surfaces through the res.partner @api.onchange('phone','country_id','company_id') hook, not through client JS.

No outbound HTTP/network calls: http_call_sites=0, sdk_imports=[], uses_api_keys=false, endpoints=[]. The sole external dependency is the in-process pure-Python `phonenumbers` library (imported in tools/phone_validation.py and patched offline in lib/phonenumbers_patch for regions BR/CI/CO/IL/KE); validation is fully local with no third-party service.

classification.rationale: phone_validation is cross-cutting master-data-quality infrastructure, not a primary value-creating activity. It owns no business object of its own beyond an opt-out list (phone.blacklist) and a reusable mixin (mail.thread.phone); its real product is a firm-wide utility — _phone_format injected onto the abstract 'base' model plus the phonenumbers wrapper — consumed by many primary modules (crm, sms, event, mass-mailing). Stabell & Fjeldstad: 'support' (firm infrastructure, like accounting/IT services), reinforced by category 'Hidden', auto_install=true, and depends only on base+mail. APQC 8.0 Manage Information Technology is chosen because the module is a data-quality / master-data correctness service (8.x covers managing information/data and its quality) that standardizes and validates a shared data attribute (the phone number) across the whole system rather than executing any line-of-business process. 3.0 Market and Sell was rejected because phone_validation performs no selling — it merely guarantees the integrity of contact data that selling/marketing modules later use; the value here is the IT-managed data utility, so 8.0 is the better single fit.
